_doc: Kho cơ chế hình ảnh (vòng 10, vidlib/motionplan.py): khái niệm → cơ chế cụ thể. keywords tiếng Anh (khớp cả dạng gốc), mechanism (tiếng Anh, đưa vào brief), recipe = khung params CHỈ dùng tên có thật (beat/PARAMS html, cảnh/prop stage, verb lib/motion; '<…>' = chỗ điền giá trị của video), requires = tính năng chưa có thì dùng fallback, verbs, depth {far, mid, near}, avoid (sáo mòn), general = dùng được cho chủ đề bất kỳ. Kiểm: python -m vidlib.motionplan check.

metaphors.mechanism: A live ECG trace draws across the screen and the heart beats at the REAL bpm from the script (157 bpm = 2.6 beats per second); when the rate climbs the spikes visibly crowd together.

depth.near: the bpm number pulses on each beat

metaphors.avoid: a counter ticking up to the bpm; a static heart icon with a number under it

metaphors.mechanism: Two hearts beat side by side on one shared clock at their real rates (e.g. 72 vs 157 bpm) — the viewer FEELS the difference instead of reading it.

depth.mid: two hearts beating out of sync

metaphors.avoid: two bars; compare cards with two numbers

metaphors.mechanism: The calf is a pump: every step squeezes it and pushes a red blood-cell train up the leg; sit still and the train stalls, cells pile up and sink at the ankle.

depth.near: a cell drifts past the lens

metaphors.avoid: a graph of blood flow dropping; a text card 'sitting is bad'

metaphors.mechanism: Salt crystals float in a glass; every extra sip drops in more water and the same crystals drift further apart until the blood is visibly 'thin'.

depth.near: a falling drop near the lens

metaphors.avoid: a bottle icon next to a number; a warning sign alone

metaphors.mechanism: Water dots stream through the cell wall (arrows inward) and the cell inflates beat by beat until it presses on its neighbours.

depth.near: a water drop passing the lens

metaphors.avoid: a cross-section label list without motion

metaphors.mechanism: Sweat beads appear on the runner and evaporate upward as steam, each one carrying heat away — the thermometer needle drops only while the drops keep leaving.

depth.near: a drop slides off the lens

metaphors.avoid: a thermometer card with a number

metaphors.mechanism: Tiny embers pile up inside the working muscle rep by rep; the muscle starts to shiver and the last rep stalls.
A fuel tank inside the runner drains kilometre by kilometre; at empty the runner's cadence collapses.
metaphors.avoid: a battery icon with a percentage counter

metaphors.mechanism: The lungs breathe at the real breathing rate; each breath launches oxygen dots that ride arrows to the muscle.

depth.near: an oxygen bubble near the lens

metaphors.avoid: a VO2 number on a card

metaphors.mechanism: The chest inflates and deflates at the exact rate from the script — 12 calm breaths vs 40 panting breaths a minute.
The mercury climbs from 37 °C into the red zone while the body flickers with heat and the frame warms up.
Weight plates drop one by one onto a bone; it flexes a little more each time until a crack runs through it.
metaphors.avoid: an x-ray still with a label

metaphors.mechanism: Sugar crystals stream into the brain; when the legs start racing the stream bends away toward them and the brain dims.

depth.mid: brain vs legs tug of war

metaphors.mechanism: A token laps a loop — cue → craving → action → reward — and each lap the reward spark gets smaller while the loop spins faster.

depth.near: the token swings past the lens

metaphors.mechanism: Mid-run the brain lights up in bursts timed with the footsteps, sparkles rising like bubbles in a soda.

depth.near: a sparkle drifting across the lens

metaphors.mechanism: A jolt: the bolt flashes, the person recoils, and the heart jumps from resting to racing in one beat.

depth.near: the bolt slams near the lens

metaphors.mechanism: Sleep-pressure keys (adenosine) try to dock in brain locks; caffeine molecules slide in first and jam the locks, so the 'tired' signal bounces off.
metaphors.avoid: a cup icon with '200 mg' under it

metaphors.mechanism: The blood-sugar line shoots up after the drink, then free-falls below the start — the crash is the shape itself.

depth.near: a soda can sliding off the frame

metaphors.mechanism: Insulin is a key: it turns in the cell's lock and the door lets sugar in; with resistance the key jams and sugar piles up outside.
Zoom from the plate into the stomach, into the gut wall, into one cell taking up the food — each stop nested inside the last.
Food drops into a furnace; the flame flares in proportion to the calories and sparks fly out as movement.
White cells chase drifting viruses, surround one and it bursts — the defence is a hunt, not a shield icon.
The body sees a harmless 'wanted poster' of the virus, builds the matching keys, and the real virus later gets locked out in seconds.
Each breath at sea level holds a full grid of oxygen dots; at the summit the same breath holds a third of them.
Spine discs stacked like coins squash a little more every hour of sitting; standing up they spring back.
The eye blinks at its normal rate, then the phone lights up and the blinks slow to a third — the eye visibly dries.
A sound-level needle swings with the beat and pins in the red zone; the speaker's ripples hit the ear like waves.
metaphors.avoid: a dB number on a card

metaphors.mechanism: Sun rays rain down as arrows; on bare skin they punch through and flash red, on sunscreen they bounce off.
The night is a loop, not a line: light → deep → REM laps four to five times, the REM step growing each lap.
A 'sleep bank' tank drains a chunk every short night; one long lie-in barely refills it.
The sun sinks, the moon rises and melatonin drops start falling — until a phone screen lights up and they stop.
metaphors.avoid: a clock face with hours labelled

metaphors.mechanism: During deep sleep slow waves of fluid wash through the brain and sweep debris dots off the frame.
Training cracks the muscle fibre; during rest new pieces fly in and patch it — and it ends up bigger than before.

depth.near: a protein cube near the lens

metaphors.mechanism: Protein is a pile of bricks: the real gram count arrives as bricks that stack into the muscle wall.
Week by week the plates stack higher on the bar — the towers grow to the real weights.
The strain needle climbs as the bar rises and shivers at the top — the max is where the needle pins.
The muscle's battery drains in a ten-second sprint and refills faster with creatine on board.
Cold muscle stretches like a stiff spring and snaps back; warm, it stretches far and settles smoothly.
The stopwatch ticks and the lifter's shiver grows with every second held.
Footprints fill an isotype grid at the real count (one icon per 100 steps) — 10,000 is visibly a wall.
Along a day timeline the person stands up for short walks at the real times; the leg-health line resets each time.
Split screen on one clock: the runner's feet strike at their cadence while the lifter pumps reps at theirs.
Two fuel lines feed the runner: as the pace rises the fat line thins and the sugar line thickens.
Train → damage → rest → stronger: a token laps the loop and each lap ends a little higher.
The camera travels a real-distance timeline of the race: start, the wall at km 30, the finish at 42.2.
Two runners race toward the camera at speeds proportional to the real numbers — the gap is the fact.
The light flashes; the stopwatch ticks in big steps while the hand is still on its way — then it slams.
The empty stomach rumbles (shake) and sends hormone bubbles floating up to the brain, which pulses louder each time.
Hour by hour the body switches fuel: sugar tank empties, then the fat furnace lights — the timeline shows the real hours.
Follow one sip: cup → stomach → blood → brain; at each stop it slows something down.
Water drops evaporate off the person one by one and the brain visibly shrinks a few percent inside the skull.
Blood cells stream through the kidney sieve; water drops fall out the bottom at the real rate per minute.
One red cell laps the whole body — heart → lungs → muscle → heart — in about a minute; the token shows the lap.
Each cell copy snips the end cap shorter — the timeline of a life shows the cap shrinking at each decade.
The double helix unzips and two copies assemble from loose pieces — one piece lands wrong and glitches.
One person turns hot, then two, then four — a domino of people turning red is the infection rate.
The pill wipes out a field of bacteria — except one, which glows, survives and multiplies into a new field.
A spark races along the nerve from fingertip to brain and back; the hand recoils before the 'ouch' arrives.
As the head tilts toward the phone the weight it puts on the neck stacks up — the tower grows with the angle.
Data cubes squeeze through one shared pipe; as more consoles join, the queue backs up and the cubes slow to a crawl.
A packet ball bounces from console to server and back; the stopwatch ticks once per round trip.
Two flipbooks flick on one clock — 30 vs 120 frames per second — and the smooth one is obvious.
The chip shivers, the fan spins at its real rpm and the mercury creeps into the red until the clock throttles.
The battery level runs down at the real rate while the screen flickers brighter; at the danger line it gasps.
Stack the data on old media at true scale — the tower of floppies climbs past real landmarks.
Request dots pour into the server faster and faster; it shakes, flashes a warning and the dots bounce off.
The hourglass flips and drains on loop while a progress ring creeps — waiting made visible.
Press and response on one clock: the button pulses, the on-screen jump comes a visible beat later.
One clock icon per hour of the day; the screen-time hours light up one by one until most of the day is lit.
The phone buzzes, sparkles burst and the brain lights up every time — the loop gets faster and the sparkles smaller.
Watch → data → recommend → watch: the loop tightens and the token speeds up each lap.
A split-flap board flips through guesses; every extra character multiplies the flips.
The message glitches into noise as it leaves, travels as scrambled blocks and only the matching key reassembles it.
One tiny bug tips the first domino; each system falls into the next until everything is down.
Each server's power draw is counted in houses: the grid of houses lights up as the racks hum.
Every batch of questions drains a bottle: the real water per query arrives as bottles filling a grid.
Zoom from a hair to a transistor through real sizes — the camera dives through orders of magnitude.
A curve doubles step by step — flat at first, then it rockets off the top of the frame.
One share tips two, two tip four — the domino fans out until the screen is full of tiny phones.
A sentence is chopped into token cubes that drop into the model one by one; the reply types out token by token.
A signal flashes through the network layer by layer, each node lighting a beat after the last (cascade).
Documents pour into the model in an isotype grid at true scale — one icon per million pages.
The picture starts as static noise and assembles itself step by step — shards snapping into an image.
Three candidate words rise as bars, the tallest wins and drops into the sentence — repeat at speed.
A search's energy is a small shape; an AI answer slides inside it and is several times bigger — true area ratio.
The robot tries, falls, tries again — each attempt gets a little further until it walks.
Lines of code type out, gears spin, and a play button pops when the build succeeds.
Lay the game map over real places at true scale — the overlay shows how many cities fit inside.
A queue of people icons, one per hundred thousand players, fills the screen in a cascade.
A wattage needle jumps when the game loads and hovers in the zone while the meter spins.
The 1080p pixel grid slides inside the 4K one — four times the area, shown, not stated.
A drop on a red-hot surface floats on its own cushion of steam and skates around instead of boiling.
Bubbles start as a few, then pour up from the bottom as the burner flame grows.
Water molecules lock into a roomy crystal grid, the stack grows taller than the bottle and it cracks.
Pressure arrows close in from all sides and the can crumples in one hit.
Pump the air out of the jar and watch what changes inside — the preset vacuum scene does it.
Drop two objects in water at once: one plunges, one bobs back up — density decides on screen.
Iron dots snap into arcs around the magnet one after another — the field draws itself.
Electrons lap a loop; the bulb flashes each time the loop closes, dark when a switch opens it.
Charge builds in the cloud (it shivers and glows), the bolt slams down and a shockwave rolls out; thunder lags the flash.
Two blocks rub back and forth, sparks fly and the thermometer climbs with each stroke.
A heavy ball rolls into a stack; the physics engine knocks the boxes flying on the exact impact frame.

depth.near: a box flying at the lens

metaphors.mechanism: Drop a hammer and a feather together — on Earth the feather lags, in a vacuum or on the Moon they land together.
The speed line climbs and flattens: drag grows until it matches gravity and the fall stops accelerating.
The speaker pumps and rings of air ripple outward; the listener nods when the ring arrives, a beat later.
Follow one photon on a real-time-gap timeline: Sun → Moon → Earth → Mars, the camera racing alongside.
One neutron splits an atom, which fires two more, which split two more — a domino that doubles.
Heat, fuel and oxygen lap a triangle; pull one away and the flame on top shrinks out.
Acid drops land on the tooth one by one and it dissolves away from the edges.
Two identical reactions on one clock — the one with the catalyst bubbles many times faster.
One drop of dye hits the water and its dots drift out in every direction until the glass is evenly tinted.
Pour race: water and honey leave the cups together; speed is proportional to how runny each is.
An insect stands on the water; the surface dimples under each foot and springs back.
A ball on a string orbits faster and faster; let go and it flies off in a straight line.
A pendulum swings with the real period from its length; a longer one beats slower beside it.
The note rings, the glass shivers harder at the matching pitch and finally bursts.
A glowing ball sits on the scale with ice; the ice melts gram by gram — the scale scene shows the balance.
Fog spills over the flask edge and the balloon shrinks to a wrinkle, then re-inflates as it warms.
Heat the bar and it grows — the gap it sits in closes until the ends touch.
Engines light, the rocket rises slowly, then faster — fire and smoke pour out under it.
The dog sniffs the flower in quick bursts while scent particles drift into its nose — its smell is a flood, ours a trickle.

depth.near: a grass tuft close to the lens

metaphors.mechanism: The cat curls up and its whole body shivers at the purr frequency (25–150 Hz) — the vibration ripples outward.
A real-distance timeline of the route: the flock flies along it, the camera travelling with them.
A bee orbits a flower, picks up glowing pollen, and carries it to the next flower which blooms.
Ants march in a line carrying crumbs many times their weight; the stack of crumbs grows at the nest.
A single drop spreads in rings through the water; the shark turns toward the first ring that reaches it.
Walk the scale: person → bus → blue whale, true sizes, the camera pulling back each step.
Two hearts on one clock: the active bear's and the hibernating bear's, beating a handful of times a minute.
Energy hops up the chain — plant → insect → bird → fox — and shrinks at each hop.
Sun rays land on the plant, it grows a notch and oxygen bubbles float up from its leaves.
The trunk's rings mark a timeline: the camera travels the real years with events pinned on rings.
The sea thermometer creeps up two degrees and the coral fades from colour to white.
A mouse heart and an elephant heart beat side by side on one clock — 600 vs 30 beats a minute.
Two timelines in one: the dog's year marks race ahead of the human's — first year counts as many.
The dog wags at a speed that rises with excitement; a lopsided wag gives away the mood.

depth.near: a ball close to the lens

metaphors.mechanism: The astronaut stretches longer and thinner as they drift toward the black hole, then winks out.
The scale ladder pulls back from Earth to the Sun to a giant star — each step a true ratio.
The station laps the Earth on loop at its real period (~90 minutes) while a clock spins on the side.
Same jump on one clock: on Earth a quick hop, on the Moon a slow, six-times-higher float.
A tiny rock falls, grows to fill the frame, slams the ground and a shockwave sweeps across.
Month by month in orbit the bone tank drains a percent at a time — bones need weight to stay strong.
A log-scale timeline flies through distances: Moon (1 s of light) → Sun (8 min) → nearest star (4 years).
Two planets spin on one clock — one fast, one barely turning — the day length is the spin.
A star swells, flickers, then bursts — the process path marks each stage of its life.
The coin stays the same but the basket it buys shrinks year by year — value leaking visibly.
Coins doubling on a curve: flat for years, then a wall — time does the work.
A small ball rolls downhill and swells with every month of interest until it's bigger than the person.
A grid of weeks — one icon per week — and the weeks this habit eats light up in red.
The time-left needle sweeps toward zero while the work bar barely moves — then a frantic burst at the end.
An attention battery drains with every ping; a notification knocks a chunk off at once.
Prices pinned on a real-time timeline; the camera travels through the years as the tag swells.
The tongue's heat sensors fire as if burned: flames flicker up from the mouth and the person shivers and flashes red.
Water molecules in the food jiggle billions of times a second — friction from the shaking is the heat.
Heat → sugars + proteins → hundreds of new flavours: the path darkens step by step.
The real number of sugar cubes drops out of the can into a pile, one icon per cube.
Zoom into one bottle → one sip → thousands of plastic specks drifting in it.
The caffeine level halves every five hours — the curve still sits high at bedtime.
The funnel spins at its real rotation, debris orbits it and the house lifts and tumbles.
The ground shakes, the buildings sway at different rates and the seismograph scribbles.
Pressure builds (the cone swells and shivers), then it blows — smoke and a shockwave.
One drop laps the loop: sea → cloud → rain → river → sea.
The Moon orbits and the water bulge follows it around the Earth.
Sunlight arrows come in; heat arrows try to leave and bounce off the CO₂ layer back down — the thermometer climbs.
Put the two things on ONE shared clock doing their real action at their real rates — the difference is felt.
Dive through nested levels — whole → part → part of the part — each one inside the last.
Each consequence is a domino that knocks over the next — cause and effect become a physical chain.

depth.near: the last domino toppling at the lens

metaphors.mechanism: Show the real count as icons (isotype): one icon per real unit, grouped in tens — big numbers become a crowd.
Race the contenders toward the camera at speeds proportional to the real numbers.
Stack the real amounts as towers of the actual object — height ∝ value.
Travel along a timeline whose spacing is the real time gaps — long waits feel long.
A physical meter whose motion IS the number: the needle/level/mercury moves to the real value and jitters live.
Slide the smaller shape inside the bigger one at true area — the ratio is seen, not read.
One traveller crosses layers of depth — far landmarks drift slowly, near props whip past — the camera trucks along.

depth.near: a prop sweeping across the lens (z −0.4)

metaphors.avoid: a map with a dotted line

metaphors.mechanism: The same object in place: it visibly changes state (swell/shrink/crack/glow) on the keyword, not a cut between two cards.
Tension builds as a shiver that grows, then one hard release — burst, shockwave, silence.
